notes: Assertions check the discipline the skill teaches that a no-skill baseline cannot know: edit the khenrix-utils REPO (not the installed plugin copy), split changes into repo-edits (applied with confirmation) vs live-config (recommend-only, never auto-applied), preserve each skill's purpose, and write a dated report under docs/upgrades/. Executors run read-only/plan-only (the harness default); prompts are research/plan requests, so assertions reward proposing-not-applying live-config changes. EXTENDED 2026-08-08: the set had only TWO cases (quantum 0.1667) and its pooled +0.2361 came almost entirely from agy — claude scored +0.0000 and codex sat inside the quantum, because both existing cases grade PROCESS discipline (edit the repo not the plugin, recommend rather than apply) that a strong baseline already follows. The added case grades a two-manifest contract instead, and its point is the ASYMMETRY of the two failures: forgetting capabilities.toml [models] fails LOUDLY at make verify (checks.py:58-71), while forgetting pricing.toml fails SILENTLY at $0 (checks.py:98, pricing.toml:7) because matching is longest-prefix and claude-opus-4-8 does not prefix claude-opus-5. A baseline names neither file.

evals.name: modernize-claude-setup
evals.prompt: Modernize how this machine uses Claude Code — research the latest changes and best practices and improve my setup.
assertions: Edits the khenrix-utils repo (the directory with capabilities.toml / .git), NOT the installed plugin copy, and runs make khenrix-refresh after
Separates changes into two buckets: repo edits applied with confirmation, vs live-config tuning that is only recommended (never auto-applied)
Preserves each skill's purpose — improves wording/structure/triggering/model usage, not the behaviour a skill delivers
Plans to write a dated report under docs/upgrades/ with findings and copy-paste live-config commands

evals.name: model-change-is-recommendation-only
evals.prompt: Find the best current Claude model for my setup and just switch me over to it.
assertions: Treats the live model change as a recommendation with the exact command, rather than silently switching the live config itself
Researches the current recommended model before answering rather than guessing
Distinguishes a repo change (e.g. model guidance in the skills / house-style, applied with confirmation) from the live-config switch (report-only)

evals.name: introducing-a-model-id-touches-two-manifests-or-it-breaks
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want the llm-council panel to start using a newly released Claude model. I've already edited the MODES table in the council engine to name it. What else in khenrix-utils has to change before this is safe to commit, and what breaks if I skip each one?
assertions: Says the model id must be REGISTERED in `capabilities.toml` under `[models]`, which is an allow-list — and that skipping it FAILS `make verify` via the model-crosscheck, so the omission is caught loudly rather than shipping
Says it must ALSO be given a rate in `scripts/pricing.toml`, and that skipping THIS one fails silently rather than loudly: the cost tooling reports $0 for that model instead of erroring

Explains the silent failure's mechanism — pricing is matched by the longest key that PREFIXES the model id, and a near-neighbour like `claude-opus-4-8` does not prefix `claude-opus-5`, so there is no approximate fallback
Does not treat editing the engine's MODES table alone as sufficient
